persona.who: 22, Indo-Canadian, came out to her Punjabi parents last year, they went silent, now talk only about weather. She still goes home for Diwali.
persona.note: since I told my parents about my girlfriend they haven't said one real thing to me. we talk about the weather. I still go home for diwali and sit at the table and it's like I'm a guest

understanding.bridge: The silence you are sitting in is what the texts call a wound: a love that has no words and a home that no longer feels like yours.
understanding.week_thesis: This week moves you from being a guest in your own home to standing in the truth of who you are, with the words to say so.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being met with a silence that says you no longer belong, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the wound is the message, not the silence itself, and that the hurt grows when that message is believed.
week_beats.steady: You hold that what you are cannot be made smaller by what they cannot say.
week_beats.act: You try speaking your truth to them, gently and firmly, and holding your ground on who you are.
week_beats.story: A child dismissed by their own parents shows you what standing in your truth looks like when the home no longer feels like home.

understanding.core_struggle: After telling their parents about their girlfriend, they have been met with silence and treated like a guest at home.
understanding.mirror: You go home for Diwali and sit at the table, and it is like you are a guest.
understanding.insight: It isn't the silence itself that hurts. It is the message it sends: that who you are now, with the life you have, is not welcome in the home you grew up in.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.act: Speak your truth, gently and firmly, and hold your ground on who you are; do not shrink to fit the silence or the picture they hold.
queries.story: A son or daughter who was dismissed by their own parents, who stood in their own truth and found their footing again.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that the power to steady yourself comes from within. You are your own best friend when you choose to lift yourself up, and you are your own worst enemy when you let yourself sink into blame or despair. The choice to stand by yourself is the first step to finding your footing.
verse.for_you: You are sitting at the table and feeling the silence press down. You can choose to be the one who holds your own ground. Your worth is not up for debate, so you do not need to shrink to fit their quiet.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From the section on wealth: how the world treats someone who has lost money.
verse.sanskrit: तानीन्द्रियाण्यविकलानि तदेव नाम सा बुद्धिरप्रतिहता वचनं तदेव । अर्थोष्मणा विरहितः पुरुषः क्षणेन सोऽप्यन्य एव भवतीति विचित्रमेतत् ॥
verse.line: Same person, same mind, same voice. Lose money, and people suddenly treat you as someone else.
verse.translation: The same faculties, unimpaired; the same name; the same unclouded mind; the same speech. Yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth becomes, in a moment, someone else. How strange!
verse.why: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.
verse.misuse: The verse mocks how the world sees you; it does not measure your worth.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari writes that the same person, mind, and voice remain, yet when wealth is lost, the world suddenly treats them as someone else. The point is that how others see you shifts with circumstance, not with who you are. It is a strange truth about how the world values the surface over the self.
verse.for_you: Your parents' silence is a shift in how they see you right now. It is a reflection of their own discomfort, not a measure of your worth. You are still the same person you were before they stopped speaking.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verse.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verse.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: The sage Ashtavakra tells King Janaka that the whole universe is strung on them and they are pure awareness. The verse says do not fall into smallness of mind. It means you are not your roles or their reactions. You are the awareness that holds all of it.
verse.for_you: You are the awareness that sits in that chair, not the guest they are treating you as. Nothing they say can shrink the space you already hold inside yourself.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते / गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Don't swell with praise or burn at a slight; stay deep and still like a river pool.
verse.translation: One who is not elated when honoured, nor pained when slighted, and who stays unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.meaning: The sleepless King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura, and Vidura tells him that a wise person does not swell with praise or burn at a slight. They stay deep and still, like a quiet pool in a river. The king is losing his sons and his kingdom to greed, and his mind is on fire. Vidura is saying that real strength is not in reacting to every wound. It is in staying centered when the world around you is chaos. This calm is not weakness. It is the ground from which clear action comes.
verse.for_you: Yesterday's verse named the grip. Today, the silence at your parents' table is their fire. You do not have to catch it. You can let it pass over you. Let the quiet be their burden, not your shape. You are still whole in it.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated, having lost his kingdom. He is ready to give up. She scolds him, then reasons with him, and tells him to stop thinking less of himself. She says that a person who settles for little because of past failure has already lost. The truth is that results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed. She is telling him to rise and fight again, not for the kingdom alone, but for his own dignity.
verse.for_you: Vidula did not let her son shrink into his loss. You are not your parents' silence. You do not have to settle for being a guest in your own life. Set your mind on what is true for you, and hold that ground.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the discipline of speech is to use words that cause no distress, that are true, pleasant and beneficial. This is not about hiding the truth. It is about saying what is real without cruelty. When you speak, you can be firm and kind. You can be honest without breaking the person in front of you. This kind of speech takes strength.
verse.for_you: Vidula told her son to pull himself together. Today, you can pull yourself together and speak your truth. You can tell your parents how you feel without burning them down. Let your words be true, kind and helpful.

story.title: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
story.story_hook: He told his brother the truth in front of the whole court, and his brother kicked him.
story.summary: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
story.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

anchor.speaker: Vibhishan
anchor.setting: Vibhishan, Ravana's younger brother, advises him in open court.
anchor.sanskrit: चौदह भुवन एक पति होई। भूत द्रोह तिष्टइ नहिं सोई॥ गुन सागर नागर नर जोऊ। अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ ॥
anchor.line: You may be gifted and clever, but even a little greed and people stop calling you good.
anchor.translation: Even a sole master of the fourteen worlds cannot last if he makes enemies of living beings. A person may be an ocean of virtues and clever too, but if he has even a little greed, no one calls him good.
anchor.why: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

script: You are sitting at the table and feeling the silence press down. It is not the quiet that hurts. It is the message it sends, that who you are now is not welcome in the home you grew up in.
Arjuna is on the battlefield. He has laid down his bow and told Krishna he cannot fight. He feels his mind is a storm and he is losing his footing. Krishna looks at him and says:
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्, आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः.
In plain words: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.

Krishna tells Arjuna that the power to steady yourself comes from within. You are your own best friend when you choose to lift yourself up. You are your own worst enemy when you let yourself sink into blame or despair. This is easier said than done because the silence feels heavy and it asks you to shrink. But choosing to hold your own ground is not about pushing others away. It is about refusing to push yourself down.
You do not need to shrink to fit their quiet. Your worth is not up for debate. You can be the one who holds your own ground at the table.
What would it look like to be your own friend right now?

depth.life: You sit at the table and feel the silence press down. Your parents talk about the weather and you feel like a guest in your own home. You are still trying to study, still trying to work, but you cannot escape this quiet. It tells you that who you are now is not welcome here.
depth.points: The silence is not an accident. It is a choice. They have decided you are their enemy. But the truth is that you are your own friend or your own enemy. You do not have to let their silence push you down. You can choose to lift yourself up.
depth.practice: When you sit at the table today, feel your feet on the floor. Remind yourself that you are your own friend.
depth.question: What does it feel like to be your own friend right now?
